\begin{center}
{\large\bfseries A ten-variable Diophantine candidate}\\
{\small Strictly positive integer unknowns; exact degree 750; 80 evaluator operations.}
\end{center}
The only unknowns are \(a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,j\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
Each \(\mathtt{r01},\ldots,\mathtt{r80}\) below is an abbreviation,
not an additional unknown. Evaluate the rows in order using ordinary integer
arithmetic; subtraction is integer subtraction, and intermediate values may be
negative. The equation is
\(\boxed{\mathtt{r80}=0}\).

\textbf{The four fixed integers.} All indices in the following formulas are
locally bound indices for constants, not unknowns. Set \(\rho=2^{67}\) and
\(\beta=\rho^{8807}-1\). Let the fixed set and ordered list be
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal S={}&\bigl(\{0,\ldots,942\}\cup\{983,\ldots,992\}\cup
\{1003,\ldots,1011\}\cup\{1013,\ldots,1031\}\\
&\quad\cup\{1063,1064,1095,2195,3296\}\bigr)\setminus\{1\},\\
\lambda={}&(1023,1024,1025,1026,1027,1028,1029,1030,1013,1014,\\
&\quad 1015,1016,1017,1018,1019,1020,1021,1003,1004,1005,\\
&\quad 1006,1007,1008,1009,1010,983,984,985,986,987,\\
&\quad 988,989,990,991,1031,1022,1011,992,1095,2195,\\
&\quad 3296).
\end{aligned}
\]
The list \(\lambda\) has 41 entries, numbered from zero. The fixed list
\(\sigma\) has 943 entries, also numbered from zero, and is printed in
decimal below and on the following pages. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu={}&\beta-\sum_{u\in\mathcal S}\rho^u-2\rho^{1063},\\
\nu={}&\beta+4+\sum_{u=1013}^{1022}\rho^u+\sum_{u=1065}^{1073}\rho^u
 +\rho^{2195}+\rho^{3296}\\
&+(2^{51}-2)(\rho^{4393}+\rho^{5495})
 +(2^{65}-1)\sum_{u=8792}^{8804}\rho^u+(2^{19}-1)\rho^{8805},\\
\kappa={}&\rho^{30}+\rho^{62}+\rho^{1100}+\rho^{2201}+\rho^{8849}\\
&+\sum_{u=0}^{942}\sigma_u(\rho^{4393-u}+\rho^{5495-u})
 +\sum_{u=0}^{40}2^{10+u}(\rho^{4393-\lambda_u}+\rho^{5495-\lambda_u}).
\end{aligned}
\]
